For a **pellet smoker**, I’d pick the **BLUETTI Elite 200 V2** if you want a comfortable overnight margin or plan to charge campsite essentials too. It has **2,073.6 Wh** of capacity and a **2,600 W inverter**; the listing says that’s enough for roughly two or three overnight cooks. [Buy the Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2) · [Specs and runtime estimate](https://dealectric.com/power-station-to-run-a-pellet-smoker-overnight)

For a lighter-duty option, the **BLUETTI AC180** has **1,152 Wh** and is listed at **$449**—enough for about one overnight cook, assuming your smoker’s actual draw is in the expected range. [AC180 listing](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180)

A 12-hour pellet cook is estimated at about **450–750 Wh**, but cold or windy conditions and other devices can cut into that. Check your smoker’s startup draw against the station’s inverter rating before buying. These recommendations are for **pellet grills**, which use electricity mainly for the auger, fan, and igniter—not electric smokers with heating elements, which need far more power. [Runtime assumptions](https://voltandvalley.com/tailgate-travel/best-power-station-for-a-pellet-grill)
